claims.note: 5845(a) is the NFA 'firearm' definition; amendment adds LTL devices to the excluded items.

claims.claim: Section 5845(a) of the Internal Revenue Code is amended by adding less-than-lethal projectile devices (as defined in Section 4182(d)(2)) and listed devices
claims.sourceSpan: any less-than-lethal projectile device (as defined in section 4182(d)(2)), any device referred to in section 4182(d)(1)(B)
claims.note: 'listed devices' = 'any device referred to in section 4182(d)(1)(B)' (the (4)(B) list).

claims.claim: to the items, such as antique firearms, excluded from the definition
claims.sourceSpan: any antique firearm
claims.note: Antique firearm is among the excluded items in 5845(a) (struck 'an antique firearm or', reinserted 'any antique firearm').

claims.claim: Directs Treasury to publish and annually report to Congress a list of non-lethal devices that would qualify except that their projectiles exceed 500 feet per second
claims.sourceSpan: make publicly available a list of devices that the Secretary has determined are not described in paragraph (2) but would be so described if such paragraph were applied without regard to subparagraph (A)(ii) thereof
claims.note: Subparagraph (A)(ii) is the 500 fps velocity prong; report to Congress confirmed at (4)(B)(ii).

claims.claim: The bill defines qualifying devices by a 500 feet-per-second projectile cap but does not exempt devices above that speed, only adds them to a monitoring list
claims.sourceSpan: any device contained on the most recent list made available by the Secretary under paragraph (4)(B)
claims.note: MATERIAL: Devices exceeding 500 fps that the Secretary places on the paragraph (4)(B) list ARE exempted -- from the excise tax via 4182(d)(1)(B), and from the National Firearms Act via 5845(a)'s reference to 'any device referred to in section 4182(d)(1)(B)'. The (4)(B) list is not merely a monitoring list; inclusion confers tax and NFA exemption. Only the Title 18 firearm-restriction exemption (Sec 102) is hard-capped at 500 fps. The gap's blanket 'does not exempt devices above that speed, only adds them to a monitoring list' inverts the bill's actual effect for a device class.

claims.claim: The bill sets up separate 90-day determinations by the Attorney General under Title I and the Secretary of the Treasury under Title II but does not require the two determinations to be consistent
claims.sourceSpan: Pursuant to a request made by the manufacturer, producer, or importer of a device for a determination as to whether such device satisfies the requirements under paragraph (2), the Secretary shall make such determination not later than 90 days after the date of receipt of such request
claims.note: Two separate 90-day tracks confirmed; text imposes no consistency requirement between them (absence).

claims.claim: The bill requires an annually updated public list of qualifying devices but sets no deadline for the first list
claims.sourceSpan: The Secretary shall make publicly available a list of devices that the Secretary has determined are described in paragraph (2) and shall update such list annually to take into account new devices
claims.note: Annual update required; no initial-publication deadline stated (absence).

claims.claim: The bill exempts shells or cartridges designed for qualifying devices but does not address ammunition that fits both a qualifying device and a conventional firearm
claims.sourceSpan: any shell or cartridge that meets the requirement of paragraph (2)(B) and is designed for use in a device referred to in subparagraph (A) or (B)
claims.note: Shell/cartridge exemption confirmed; text does not address dual-fit ammunition (absence).

notes: Hostile source-only audit against the engrossed (EH) bill text; referencedSources empty. CR floor quotes (criticisms/featured_quotes) were NOT audited here -- no Congressional Record source text is available to verify them against (source-only scope). One MATERIAL flag: gaps[0] claims the bill does not exempt >500 fps devices ('only adds them to a monitoring list'), but 4182(d)(1)(B) exempts (4)(B)-listed >500 fps devices from the excise tax and 5845(a) exempts them from the NFA; only the Title 18 restriction exemption is hard-capped at 500 fps.
